newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool indicator slumps by 10c/kg.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool indicator slumps by 10c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market tumbled 10 cents on Tuesday at auction in Sydney to end at 564 cents a kg clean, Wool International (WI) said.
The market fell sharply despite principal Japanese interest coupled with support from most sectors of the trade, WI said.
In merinos, 19 micron was up to 3.5 percent cheaper, while 20/21/26 microns were three percent cheaper.
WI also said 23 micron was up to one percent dearer, with 24 micron slightly cheaper and 25 micron one percent cheaper.
In merino skirtings, 19 to 22 microns were one percent cheaper.
For crossbreds, 27 micron was 0.5 percent cheaper and 28 micron two percent cheaper, WI said.
In cardings, locks were 1.5 percent cheaper and crutchings were up to one percent cheaper.
Of the 14,464 bales offered, 13.6 percent were passed in, WI said.
Sales continue on Wednesday in Sydney and Geelong, with about 28,000 bales on offer, WI said.
